skill.name: srs-documentation

skill.summary: Create IEEE 830 Software Requirements Specification documents with templates and validation checklists.

content.value_statement: Requirements teams need consistent SRS documents that are complete, traceable, and testable. This skill provides an IEEE 830 structure, templates, and validation checklists.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of IEEE 830 SRS sections from introduction through appendices.
Provides a reusable template for scope, interfaces, requirements, constraints, and sign-off.
Defines ID conventions for functional requirements, non-functional requirements, and constraints.
Applies writing guidance for clear, verifiable requirement statements.
Includes SMART, INVEST, traceability, and document quality checklists.
Supports requirement-to-test and business objective traceability matrices.
limitations: Does not interview stakeholders or discover requirements by itself.
Does not validate technical feasibility against a live system.
Requires project details before producing a useful final SRS.
May need changes for organization-specific standards or regulated domains.

use_cases.title: Draft a Formal SRS
use_cases.description: Turn stakeholder notes into a structured IEEE 830 Software Requirements Specification.

use_cases.title: Standardize Feature Requirements
use_cases.description: Convert feature ideas into prioritized, testable functional and non-functional requirements.

use_cases.title: Prepare Test Traceability
use_cases.description: Map requirements to business objectives and planned test cases before approval.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic SRS
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new requirements document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the srs-documentation skill to create an IEEE 830 SRS for [project]. Ask for missing scope, stakeholders, constraints, and requirements before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Requirement Statements
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these requirements with the SRS writing guidelines. Rewrite vague items into testable shall statements with IDs, priority, source, and acceptance criteria: [requirements].

prompt_templates.title: Compile a Requirements Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced document generation from mixed notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compile these stakeholder notes into an SRS using template.md. Include functional requirements, non-functional requirements, assumptions, dependencies, glossary, and open issues: [notes].

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Trace an SRS
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this SRS against checklists.md. Produce a gap list, quality score, traceability matrix, unresolved risks, and recommended revisions: [SRS].

output_examples.input: Create an SRS outline for a customer support portal.
output_examples.output: An IEEE 830 outline with purpose, scope, product perspective, user classes, interfaces, requirements sections, glossary, and traceability appendices.

output_examples.input: Rewrite vague checkout requirements into testable statements.
output: Requirement statements with stable IDs and shall language.
Priorities, sources, inputs, outputs, error handling, and acceptance criteria.
Notes for any missing stakeholder or measurement details.

output_examples.input: Review this draft SRS for approval readiness.
output_examples.output: A checklist-based review covering completeness, SMART quality, traceability, document consistency, open issues, and recommended revisions.

best_practices: Provide stakeholder goals, constraints, user classes, and known integrations before drafting.
Assign stable IDs, priorities, sources, and acceptance criteria to every requirement.
Run the validation checklists before requesting stakeholder approval.
anti_patterns: Treating vague product goals as final requirements.
Mixing implementation design decisions into requirement statements too early.
Leaving TBD items, duplicate IDs, or missing sources in the final SRS.

faq.question: What standard does this skill follow?
faq.answer: It follows the IEEE 830 Software Requirements Specification structure.

faq.question: Can it create a complete SRS from short notes?
faq.answer: It can draft a structure, but useful output requires scope, stakeholders, constraints, and requirements.

faq.question: Does it cover non-functional requirements?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes performance, security, reliability, usability, and maintainability requirement sections.

faq.question: Can it help with traceability?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes traceability matrices for business objectives, requirements, dependencies, and test cases.

faq.question: Is this only for business analysts?
faq.answer: No. Product managers, architects, QA teams, and delivery leads can also use it.

faq.question: Does it execute commands or scan systems?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides documentation guidance, templates, and checklists.
